newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court orders five police arrested for killing.
newsitem.headline: Turk court orders five police arrested for killing.

text.p: A Turkish court on Wednesday ordered that five policemen on trial for the beating death of a leftist journalist be taken into custody while the case continues.
"We have decided that five of the defendant policemen should be arrested," Judge Kamil Serif told the court.
Forty-eight policemen are on trial in the western town of Afyon for the killing in January, 1996 of reporter Metin Goktepe but none of the accused had been detained.

Goktepe was among scores of people rounded up at random from an identity check after the funerals of two far-left jail inmates in Istanbul. An autopsy report shows he died from wounds consistent with beatings.
Court prosecutors have demanded 15-year jail sentences for 11 of the policemen, charged with manslaughter, who were allegedly directly involved with beating Goktepe to death.
No formal plea is needed under Turkish law and none of the policemen has appeared at several hearings of the case.
